Subject: Dedicated sizing — memory vs perf constraints (Vertex Labs)

Hi Dev,

Quick note from our infra team: our inference pipeline has two distinct profiles — (A) long-context extraction jobs that need 80–120GB of GPU memory and tolerate 300–600ms p90, and (B) high-concurrency chat routing with short context where 64B tokens bursts are common and we need <120ms p95.

We want Redwood Dedicated to cover both without severe overprovisioning. Can you recommend a SKU mix (H100 / A100 / L4) and an operational plan for slot-tiling, prefix caching, and fallthrough so we can budget and commit? Also, any constraints around multi-model fallback or quantization impacts would be helpful.

Thanks — Ayesha
Ayesha Khan
Head of Infrastructure, Vertex Labs

Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing — memory vs perf constraints (Vertex Labs)

Ayesha — thanks for the clear profile. Summary below plus an attached workbook (vertex_capacity_workbook.xlsx) with detailed sims. High level recommendations: 

1) SKU mix (starter target for 1.0 commit)
   - H100 (80% memory-heavy slots): 20% of fleet. Use for long-context extraction jobs that need >80GB memory (bert-like batches, LTR). H100 gives the memory headroom and NVLink benefits for multi-GPU model sharding when you need >context-size single-GPU memory.
   - A100 80GB (balanced slots): 50% of fleet. Good middle-ground — better throughput for many transformer models vs L4, and cheaper than H100 for moderate context sizes.
   - L4 (cost-optimized slots): 30% of fleet. Use for short-context, high-concurrency chat traffic; leverage 4-bit quantization for many customer models if acceptable.

Rationale: You want memory headroom for profile A without ballooning cost. H100 is required for the worst-case single-GPU memory footprints and for multi-gpu sharding tests; A100 covers most production traffic with reasonable cost; L4 is excellent for high QPS, short-context inference where quantization and batching shine.

2) Slot-tiling and batching policy
   - Reserve H100 slots for pinned long-context jobs (no aggressive packing). Use large continuous slots and avoid time-slicing to prevent KV cache thrash.
   - For A100 and L4, enable tiling: group short-context chat into micro-batches with dynamic padding and continuous batching windows of ~20–40ms to hit throughput targets without violating p95 SLO.

3) Caching and prefix strategy
   - Prefix/KV caching for profile B is very effective: maintain warm slots on A100 where you can use cached KV for repeated user sessions. L4 should be used for stateless bursts only unless you accept increased miss rates.

4) Quantization and quality tradeoffs
   - L4 + 4-bit quant is cost-effective but expect a small drop in some QA and extraction tasks. For profile A extraction (high-fidelity) keep H100/A100 float or 8-bit quantization. Run evaluation prompts in the workbook to quantify specific regressions.

5) Fallthrough and graceful degradation
   - Primary routing: prefer exact SKU match by policy (memory > latency > cost). Fallback order: A100 -> L4 for short-context (with prompts truncated), and H100 -> A100 for long-context (if sharding allowed). Implement automatic truncation and a soft degrade message to users when fallthrough truncates context.

6) Canary and rollout plan
   - Start with 10% of traffic to the L4 pool for non-critical chat tests for 2 weeks, measure latency and quality. Then stage 15% of extraction jobs to A100 with 8-bit quant to validate quality. Full commit only after eval pass. See attached canary_run_plan.md.

I've attached the workbook with per-model sims, costing, and a recommended reserve/capacity ladder. Marcus — did you want to add ops-level constraints (scheduling, preemption)? Soojin — can you confirm the default autoscale/burst policy we should prescribe?

— Dev

Adding ops notes / constraints: 

- Preemption: mark H100 slots non-preemptible for long-context pinned workloads. A100 can accept preemptible burst instances for cost-smoothing, but avoid if you expect long-running KV warm sessions.
- Autoscale windowing: set conservative scale-up cooldowns (30s) and faster scale-down (120s) to avoid oscillation with bursty chat traffic.
- Node packing: prefer node-level isolation for customer-critical models to meet compliance; don't mix high-compute multi-tenant jobs on the same host as pinned long-context VMs.
- Monitoring hooks: add a model-quality smoke test that runs every 6 hours on the H100 pool for extraction models to detect regression from quantization/opt kernels.

I'll sync with infra to ensure the slot reservations and node labels are applied before your canary cutover.
